text:
sara: quick sync — we need a decision on soft 'fallthrough' ordering by customer class. current behavior: when primary variant is saturated or slow we fallback to lower-cost variant. but teams want different tradeoffs per plan.

ian: agree. high level: free -> cheapest stable model, pro -> balance cost+latency, enterprise -> prefer latency even at higher cost.

mike: +1 but we also need quota semantics spelled out. do we deduct full token cost when we fallthrough? or charge at the served variant rate?

anna: from billing side - we can charge based on the actual variant that served. but product asked for an optional "grace token" pool for pro tiers so short fallthroughs don't spike invoices.

raj: telemetry ask: we need metrics for fallthrough_count{plan,region,route,from_variant,to_variant} and fallthrough_latency_p95. otherwise ops can't triage.

ian: proposal sketch (pseudo-config):
```json
{
  "plan_rules": [
    { "plan": "free", "ordering": ["variant-lowcost","variant-quantized"], "soft_fallthrough": true },
    { "plan": "pro", "ordering": ["variant-lowlat","variant-lowcost"], "soft_fallthrough": true, "grace_tokens": 10000 },
    { "plan": "enterprise", "ordering": ["variant-lowlat","variant-highperf"], "soft_fallthrough": false }
  ]
}
```

anna: two UX notes: 1) console needs an explicit preview to show effective ordering per tenant, 2) a canary toggle per plan for 7 days.

mike: runtime implications: soft_fallthrough true => return code 200 with header `x-fallthrough: soft` and metric tag. soft means we tried primary for up to N ms then routed. hard/failover means immediate replacement. need consistent semantics in API.

raj: for telemetry let's name metrics: `inference.fallthrough.count`, `inference.fallthrough.latency.p95`, `inference.fallthrough.charge_rate` and expose them to dashboards by plan. add alert: if fallthrough_count_rate for enterprise > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> page.

ian: edge case: region mismatch. if enterprise primary exists only in us-west but traffic is eu, should we fallthrough to a eu lowlat variant or keep cross-region highperf? Suggest per-tenant policy: prefer region-local variants unless plan==enterprise and cross-region latency < 50ms.

anna: console: show a decision path example and cost delta estimator for a sample workload. ops want simulated token burn for 1k reqs.

mike: implementation detail — keep routing decision stateless where possible: algorithm -> candidate list from config -> check capacity/latency SLA -> select. But capacity checks need fast distributed capacity view (LRU cache with 2s TTL).

raj: telemetry additions: tag each request with `routing_reason` values: primary_ok, soft_fallthrough, hard_fallback, region_preference, quota_blocked. makes postmortems easier.

sara: permissions/rollout: only ops + product can edit plan_rules. devex should get read & preview. put schema validation in console.

mike: sample error header for quota interplay: `x-quota-status: consumed=9500/10000;grace=500` so clients can show a warning.

anna: billing follow-up: need a short doc describing how grace_tokens are billed and how refunds are handled if a fallthrough triggers a cheaper variant.

deploy-bot: config pushed to staging at 3001112235 by ian, run id=stg-8821 :white_check_mark:

ian: next steps: I'll open a PR with config schema + runtime change list. mike will prototype capacity cache. raj will draft dashboards + alerts. anna will write billing note. sara will coordinate policy for enterprise/regional exception.

sara: sounds good. if nobody objects, we'll lock shape by EOD and start canary on staging tomorrow. :eyes:
